issues.title: [Bug]: XML template with a mismatched end tag is accepted
issues.reasoning: Spec 6.6.2 parses the template with the XML `content` production; XML WFC Element Type Match is violated, so this must be a compile-time error. Nutcracker's front end accepts it and silently drops the bad end tag. Clean-context spec check agreed (high confidence). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: duplicate attribute in an XML template is accepted and the last value wins
issues.reasoning: XML WFC Unique Att Spec (and Namespaces in XML §6.3) is violated, so the template must be rejected at compile time (spec 6.6.2). The front end accepts it and the last value wins. Per the issue, the interpolated variant panics at runtime instead, which is a consequence of the same missing front-end check. Clean-context spec check agreed (high). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: predefined `xml` prefix rejected in XML templates (`xml:lang`)
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: undefined XML namespace prefix 'xml'
 --> 1589.bal:5:32
  |
5 |     xmllib:Element e = xml `<a xml:lang="en"/>`;
  |                                ^^^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: The `xml` prefix is bound by definition (Namespaces in XML §3), and the Ballerina spec excludes it from the synthesized namespace attributes. The front end rejects it with a SEMANTIC_ERROR. Clean-context spec check agreed (medium-high). Related to #1226 (xmlns="" in templates) but that is a different problem, so this is not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML attribute values are not whitespace-normalized (tab/newline kept)
issues.reasoning: Spec 6.6.2 uses the attribute's Infoset [normalized value], and XML §3.3.3 normalizes a literal TAB to a space. The template is parsed statically, so the literal value comes from the front end and this is categorised as frontend. Note: per the issue, xml:fromString has the same defect, which would be a langlib follow-up. Clean-context spec check agreed (medium-high). Related to #1091, which covers a different rule.

issues.title: [Bug]: `new C(args)` with an isolated init is not an isolated expression (rejected as isolated variable initializer)
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: initializer of an isolated variable must be an isolated expression
  --> 1591.bal:11:20
   |
11 | isolated Box box = new Box(3);
   |                    ^^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Spec 6.8.2 says explicit-new-expr is isolated when init is isolated and all arguments are isolated, so this is a valid initializer for an isolated module variable (§8.7). The front end rejects the valid program. Clean-context spec check agreed (high). Related to #1076, #1429 and #1501 (other expression kinds not recognised as isolated), but none of them duplicates this.

issues.title: [Bug]: init method can be called on a receiver other than self
issues.reasoning: Spec 6.8.1.5: init can be called in a method-call-expr only when the receiver is `self`. The type checker accepts `a.init()` and re-runs init. Clean-context spec check agreed (high). Related to #1572 (self.init reentry), but that is a different case.

issues.title: [Bug]: operators reject a variable narrowed by removing a mutable structured type
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: union types not supported for +
 --> 1593.bal:7:12
  |
7 |     return x + 1;
  |            ^^^^^

error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: values are not comparable
  --> 1593.bal:11:27
   |
11 |     return x !is int[] && x > "a";
   |                           ^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Under §7.12 narrowing, (int[]|int) minus int[] gives int and (int[]|string) minus int[] gives string, so the + and > operators are valid. The type checker rejects the valid program. Clean-context spec check agreed (high). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: removing an already-returned list member during foreach skips members and panics
issues.output:
1
3
error: invalid array index: 2
        at main(1594.bal:5)
issues.reasoning: §5.7.1 allows removing a member the iterator has already returned, so next() must not panic and should continue with 2 and 3. The program compiles, but the interpreter skips 2 and panics with an index error. Clean-context spec check agreed (no panic: high; exact 1,2,3 sequence: medium-high). Related to #1218 (the opposite direction), not a duplicate. The issue also notes corpus test to-stream-shrink-p.bal may encode the wrong expectation.

issues.title: [Bug]: untyped listener declaration rejected when initializer type includes error
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: listener initializer is not a listener
  --> 1595.bal:33:1
   |
33 | public listener a = mk("a");
   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: §8.3.1 allows a listener-decl expression of static type L|E, and without a type-descriptor the variable has type L. The front end rejects the valid program with 'listener initializer is not a listener'. Clean-context spec check agreed (high). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: computed key in a constant mapping constructor gives UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR
issues.output:
fatal[UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR]: constant computed mapping key not implemented
 --> 1616.bal:3:13
  |
3 | const M = {["a"]: 1};
  |             ^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: A mapping constructor is a structural-constructor-expr allowed in a const-expr, and the computed key "a" is itself a const-expr, so the program is valid and should print {"a":1}. The front end emits fatal[UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR], which is a diagnostic and not a crash, so frontend-crash does not apply. Clean-context spec check agreed (medium-high). Open PR #1193 (computed mapping keys) lists this as a non-goal. Related to #987, not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: http setTextPayload on a received response keeps the backend Content-Length
issues.output:
/textNoRead cl=20000 body=[ERR:unexpected EOF]
/textAfterRead cl=20000 body=[ERR:unexpected EOF]
issues.reasoning: ballerina/http standard library bug: setTextPayload replaces the entity, but the stale backend Content-Length is still forwarded, so clients see a truncated body (RFC 9110 §8.6). Reproduced on current main with a local backend. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: TOML parser hangs on a crafted Ballerina.toml
issues.reasoning: The TOML parser loops forever on malformed Ballerina.toml instead of reporting a syntax error, so the project can never be compiled to BIR. This is categorised as frontend (project loading/parsing). It hangs rather than crashing, so frontend-crash is not added. The issue identifies a probable cause: the unbounded lookahead in looksLikeTableHeader/lookAheadForCloseBracket against peekK's 20-token cap. No duplicate found.
